author: MAITREE BARAL
description: Diabetic retinopathy often progresses quietly, leading to significant eye damage before symptoms are detected. Therefore, routine eye exams are imperative for early identification, even if one's vision appears normal. Studies show a strong link between how long a person has diabetes and their risk of developing vision issues. Consistently managing blood sugar levels and health can help avert major vision loss.
title: India's diabetes burden is creating another problem: The growing threat to eyesight

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: In response to concerns over a second suspected plague case linked to a worker's death, Russia has denied these allegations. The World Health Organization is looking for more details on the illness that led to the worker's pneumonia. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov denounced many media reports as false. Health officials assure the public that there is no epidemic threat while WHO seeks more information to evaluate health risks.
title: Russia rejects second plague scare as WHO demands answers over Siberian lab deaths

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: As tensions escalate in the Middle East, particularly around the Strait of Hormuz, oil prices have surged amid fears of potential supply disruptions. Recent assaults on tankers heighten the danger of transporting crude through this vital corridor. Additionally, American crude inventories are dwindling, signaling a tighter market, while diesel and jet fuel stocks remain below average levels, a trend seen for over seven months since the onset of regional conflict.
title: Oil remains beyond $100 per barrel as Middle East supply concerns persist

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: Young children often engage in repetitive activities, like lining up their toys, to make sense of their surroundings. This might appear peculiar at first glance; however, it serves as a valuable learning process. Parents should take note of their child's responses when changes occur in their play setup. If a child seems particularly upset, it may signal the need for a deeper developmental assessment.
title: Why some kids line up toys instead of playing, per psychology

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Northern lights may return across parts of the US and Canada overnight October 8-9 as a CME reaches Earth after an M1.4 solar flare. NOAA forecasts G1 to G2 geomagnetic storm conditions, with activity potentially strengthening early Friday. Alaska, Canada and northern US states have the best viewing chances under dark skies.
title: Northern lights may light up US, Canada tonight amid G1-G2 storm

author: PRISHA PATNAIK
title: Texas carries out first US execution since Christa Pike's botched lethal injection

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: The Pentagon has been instructed to prepare for possible military actions against Iran, amid stalled diplomatic efforts. Preparations may lead to attacks on Iranian nuclear facilities and strategic sites, although no attack timeline has been set. This situation overlaps with renewed fighting in Yemen, where Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have intensified. Meanwhile, elections in the US and Israel may influence military decisions in the region.
title: US to strike Iran? Pentagon orders military to gear up for attacks

author: AMIT KUMAR
description: Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return to India’s T20I squad has received strong backing from former India batter Wasim Jaffer, who believes the experienced pacer’s selection is based on his performances and fitness, rather than any favour. Bhuvneshwar, 36, has been recalled for India’s five-match T20I series against New Zealand, beginning October 22. Jaffer feels the veteran seamer should have been brought back into the national setup earlier.
title: 'Unko select karke koi meherbani nahi ki': Wasim on Bhuvneshwar's India return

author: MOHAMMED AKHEF
description: In a tragic incident, Mahesh Shelke, the sales manager for IndianOil, was fatally stabbed during an altercation at a petrol pump as he sought to take control of the outlet amid a dispute. Swift action was taken by authorities, resulting in the arrest of five individuals, including members of the Pandavveer family. IndianOil and the petroleum ministry have rallied to support Shelke's family during this devastating period.
title: 'Stabbed 7 times': How bid to seal petrol pump turned deadly for IndianOil official

author: G S DHANUSH
description: Three individuals, including two children, lost their lives when a building collapsed in Seemapuri, Delhi. Rescue teams responded promptly to the scene, searching for survivors and assisting the injured. Local residents reported that the structure had developed cracks after an earthquake a day earlier. The building reportedly belonged to the Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board and was around 20-25 years old.
title: ‘Cracks after quake’: Pregnant woman, 2 kids dead in Delhi building collapse

author: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK
description: Nana Patekar has passed away at his residence in Goa at the age of 75. He made significant contributions to both Hindi and Marathi cinema over several decades. Patekar was known for his powerful performances and distinctive screen presence in numerous films. Throughout his career, he received multiple National Awards and a Padma Shri for his work in the arts.
title: Veteran actor Nana Patekar passes away at 75

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: In 2025, Swiss startup Sun-Ways installed 48 removable solar panels across 100 metres of active railway tracks in Buttes. More than 11,000 trains have since passed over the installation, which has generated over 16,000 kWh of electricity. The three-year pilot is testing whether unused railway space can safely produce renewable energy without disrupting operations.
title: Swiss solar panels on railway tracks survive 11,000 trains, generate 16,000 kWh

author: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK
description: Ajay Devgn's film 'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion' continues to perform strongly at the box office. It recorded earnings of Rs 15.50 cr on its sixth day, accumulating a total of Rs 232.50 cr net in India. The movie, which opened with Rs 62.00 cr, has reached a worldwide gross of Rs 366.50 cr. Its performance over six days led to over 9.5 million footfalls globally.
title: 'Drishyam 3' Day 6: Ajay Devgn's film earns Rs 15.50cr, India total hits Rs 232.50cr

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: María del Carmen Abascal, known as Maricarmen, died in a hospital after being evicted from her home. Her eviction triggered nationwide protests highlighting the housing crisis afflicting Spain. Activists voiced anger over Maricarmen's death as a symbol of the struggle against rising rents and evictions. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez offered condolences, acknowledging the impact of her case on public sentiment.
title: 'Fight goes on’: 87-yr-old woman dies after becoming symbol of Spain housing crisis

author: TOI BUSINESS DESK
description: The case involves a dispute over whether properties that had come to the woman’s father from her grandfather retained the character of ancestral property, giving her a right to seek partition under the Hindu Succession Act. The woman, based in the US, has been living abroad since her marriage in 1979. She filed a suit seeking partition of family properties and an equal share in them after her father sold one property.
title: US-based woman files case against parents for property share; Karnataka HC rejects it

author: SHUBHANSHU DWIVEDI
description: India beat Pakistan by 19 runs to win the men’s cricket gold medal at the Asian Games last week.
title: 'Satisfied with my runs': Pakistan batter opens up on Asian Games final loss to India

author: AMIT KUMAR
description: Naman Dhir had scored 318 runs in IPL 2026 but did not bowl a single over during the tournament. His international debut showed that he can offer India another option with the ball. Former India cricketer and 1983 World Cup winner Krishnamachari Srikkanth believes Dhir’s emergence could seriously hurt Washington Sundar’s chances in white-ball cricket.
title: 'Naman Dhir has finished him': World Cup winner's big statement on star's T20I future

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: Delhi Police is reviewing videos to identify protesters involved in the alleged assault during a Congress protest. Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi were detained for defying police orders while attempting to proceed to Jantar Mantar. Police are also taking action against misleading social media posts regarding their conduct during the protest. Earlier, an FIR was lodged against Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi for forcibly entering Akashvani Bhawan.
title: Delhi Police likely to file FIR over alleged assault on police during Congress protest

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: Archaeologists investigating Turkey’s Mount Ararat have drilled the boat-shaped Durupinar formation for the first time, collecting hundreds of soil samples from depths of up to 60 feet. Researchers are examining organic matter and possible traces of ancient wood for clues linked to Noah’s Ark, but laboratory analysis is still needed before drawing conclusions.
title: Archaeologists drill 60 feet into Mount Ararat site in Noah’s Ark search

author: ANJALI SINGH
description: Athletes training at Tau Devi Lal Stadium faced significant disruption when a helicopter landed on the tracks for four days due to mechanical issues. This pattern of interruptions has alarmed the sports community, which is now urging for the establishment of a dedicated helipad. While solutions for a helihub are being considered, ensuring that athletes can train without disruption continues to be a primary concern.
title: Haryana CM’s chopper parked in Gurgaon stadium, athletes lost access to tracks for 4 days

author: KORIDE MAHESH
description: The Telangana Waqf Board is dealing with issues related to fake no-objection certificates and forged occupancy rights certificates. These forged documents are allegedly being used to illegally acquire waqf land and secure approvals. In one instance, a fake NOC was presented to a district collector regarding land ownership. Officials are warning government agencies against accepting such fraudulent documents for any official transactions.
title: Inside waqf land grab in Telangana: Fake NOCs, forged ORCs

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: Wētāpunga, the largest giant wētā species in New Zealand, is rebounding after years of decline caused by habitat destruction and invasive predators. Thanks to dedicated conservation efforts, more than 11,000 wētāpunga have been bred and released into protected areas. With at least four generations now thriving in the wild, the program aims to sustain their growing populations and ensure their future survival.
title: 11,000 wētāpunga released over 15 years now thriving on two islands

author: DHANANJAY MAHAPATRA
description: Supreme Court has agreed to hear the application from the Centre regarding Tadasha Mishra's appointment as Jharkhand DGP. The appointment has been challenged due to its conflict with procedures set in the SC's 2006 Prakash Singh judgement. Moreover, the Centre claimed that prior DGP appointments in Jharkhand were also illegal for similar reasons. Mishra's appointment occurred shortly before her retirement, which raised legal concerns.
title: Centre cites Supreme Court order, seeks to void Jharkhand DGP appointment

author: AMBIKA PANDIT
description: TMC chairperson Mamata Banerjee's arrival in Delhi has heightened anticipation for the requested meeting with President Droupadi Murmu. The opposition bloc is awaiting confirmation for a meeting date between October 7 and 9. The delegation has been limited to ten members as requested by the President's Secretariat. CPI(M)'s John Brittas has submitted a petition for constitutional intervention regarding the Election Commission.
title: Mamata Banerjee’s Delhi arrival fuels buzz over INDIA bloc meet with President

author: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK
description: In 2007, Sandra Bullock acquired a sprawling 91-acre ranch in Valley Center for $2.725 million. After transforming it with extensive renovations and establishing an organic avocado farm, she sold the property for $5.6 million in 2024. Encompassing a beautifully refurbished adobe house, a guest cottage, and facilities for agricultural operations, the ranch stands as a perfect blend of luxury and sustainability for its future owner.
title: Sandra Bullock’s 91-acre California ranch with 1,200 avocado trees sells for $5.6m

author: DHANANJAY MAHAPATRA
description: Supreme Court has maintained the condition for Rajpal Yadav to deposit Rs 2 crore for his appeal. Yadav took a loan of Rs 5 crore in 2010 for a film that never completed, which has accrued interest. His counsel mentioned he secured Rs 1.15 crore and aims to sell property to cover remaining dues. The court suggested producing a successful film may help him repay the debts.
title: Make a good film, repay your debts: Supreme Court to Rajpal Yadav

author: ANUJA JAISWAL
description: National Medical Commission has issued guidelines restricting the use of AI in medical advertising and patient testimonials. Registered medical practitioners and hospitals must not engage in creating synthetic content or manipulating search rankings. Claims of being the best or offering guaranteed results are also prohibited under these rules. Additionally, offering discounts or referrals that encourage unnecessary consultations is not allowed.
title: Doctors, hospitals can't use AI to create testimonials: National Medical Commission

author: VISHWA MOHAN
description: A global decline of 73% in monitored wildlife populations occurred between 1970 and 2022. India has successfully improved populations of tigers, one-horned rhinos, and Ganga river dolphins. The report highlights threats like habitat loss, climate change, and pollution affecting wildlife. Despite the negative trends, about half of monitored populations are stable or increasing globally. Targeted conservation efforts in India demonstrate the potential for wildlife recovery and biodiversity preservation.
title: Living Planet Report: WWF finds 73% global wildlife decline; India shows recovery gains

author: SAURABH SINHA
description: Elon Musk has claimed that certain oligarchs are obstructing Starlink's entry into the Indian market. Starlink has already established the necessary infrastructure and is prepared to launch its services. The company aims to provide affordable broadband connectivity to areas lacking internet access. Regulatory approvals are awaited before the commercial rollout can commence in India. Collaboration with local telecom operators has been a key element in Starlink's strategy for success.
title: Some oligarchs blocking entry of Starlink in India: Elon Musk

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Hollywood actor Jason Scott Lee transformed 25 acres of damaged Hawaiian land into a simple, self-sufficient home. The property was once littered with car parts, paint cans and debris. Lee grew taro, raised chickens and embraced natural farming while working to restore the rainforest, reflecting his decision to pursue a simpler life away from Hollywood.
title: Hollywood actor buys 25 acres of damaged Hawaiian land to restore rainforest
